caption:
On a shared laptop or a college lab computer, the next person can press Back and read the previous user's orders.

Logging out usually clears the cookie and sends you to /login. But the browser may still hold the orders page in its back/forward cache, or the page and its API response in the HTTP cache. Press Back and it shows that copy without asking the server, so your logged-in check never runs.

Fix it on the server. Send Cache-Control: no-store on pages and API responses with personal data, so the browser doesn't keep a copy. On the logout response, Clear-Site-Data: "cache" also clears what's already stored.

Source: MDN, Cache-Control (no-store) and Clear-Site-Data.
